question.problem:
Apples produced by a particular farm are of three varieties: $1,2,$ and $3.$

- $30%$ of the apples are of variety $1,$ and $45%$ of those apples weight more than $200\,g.$

- $20%$ of the apples are of variety $2,$ and $15%$ of those apples weight more than $200\,g.$

- $50%$ of the apples are of variety $3,$ and $10%$ of those apples weight more than $200\,g.$

If $75%$ of apples from the farm are sold to a local supermarket, and $20%$ of apples sold to the supermarket weigh more than $200\,g,$ what is the probability that a randomly chosen apple that weighs more than $200\,g$ is sold to the supermarket? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let $S$ be the event that an apple is sold to the supermarket, $W$ be the event that the apple weights more than $200\,g,$ and ${V}_{1},{V}_{2},{V}_{2}$ be the events that an apple is of variety $1,$ $2,$ or $3,$ respectively. 

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

- From the bullet points, we have the following information:

$$
\begin{aligned} & P({V}_{1})=0.3 &  & P(W|{V}_{1})=0.45 \\  & P({V}_{2})=0.2 &  & P(W|{V}_{2})=0.15 \\  & P({V}_{3})=0.5 &  & P(W|{V}_{3})=0.1\end{aligned}
$$

The disjoint union ${V}_{1}⊔{V}_{2}⊔{V}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space, and we have

$$
P({V}_{1})+P({V}_{2})+P({V}_{3})=0.3+0.2+0.5=1.
$$

- Since $75%$ of apples from the farm are sold to a local supermarket, we have

$$
P(S)=0.75.
$$

- Since $20%$ of apples sold to the supermarket weigh more than $200\,g,$ we have

$$
P(W|S)=0.2.
$$

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen apple that weigh more than $200\,g$ is sold to the supermarket, which is represented as $P(S|W).$ 

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(S|W) & =\frac{P(W|S)P(S)}{P(W)} \\  & =\frac{P(W|S)P(S)}{P(W|{V}_{1})P({V}_{1})+P(W|{V}_{2})P({V}_{2})+P(W|{V}_{3})P({V}_{3})} \\  & =\frac{(0.2)(0.75)}{(0.3)(0.45)+(0.2)(0.15)+(0.5)(0.1)} \\  & =\frac{0.15}{0.215} \\  & ≈0.698,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
